lineage: follows agent-loom-e10 (fresh_execution_affordance_replication); same schema shape, adapted for a non-peer collaborator
question: How should Claude and Jev be put to work together, and on what class of decision-making problems does the pairing outperform Claude alone or a scripted-policy-plus-Jev pairing?
structural_note: Jev is not a peer arm to Claude. Claude is an autonomous agent (proposes its own actions, can be denied, retries, decides when done). Jev makes exactly one typed judgment per call and stops: it cannot enumerate options, apply an action, or manage state. 'jev_only' therefore means 'code-driven scripted policy that owns the loop, with Jev supplying the one judgment the code can't make itself' -- not 'an autonomous Jev agent'. This must be stated in any write-up of results, not just in this file.

environment.kind: text-based grid/room navigation with a declared goal
environment.legal_actions: enumerable by code at every step (no free-form action space)

level_design.straightforward: unambiguous room descriptions, single obviously-correct path, used to check baseline competence and to watch for ceiling effects (E10 saturated at 100% pass on both arms and only showed an effect on a secondary metric -- expect the same risk here)
level_design.ambiguous: deliberately misleading room descriptions (a promising-sounding dead end, two equally plausible exits where only one is correct) -- this is where calibrated judgment is hypothesized to earn its keep
level_design.optimal_path_length: computed by code (BFS/Dijkstra over the level graph) for every level, used as ground truth for path efficiency, not estimated

claude_autonomous.description: Claude sees the state each turn and outputs the next action directly. Full autonomy: no Jev, no code-level judgment gate.
claude_autonomous.execution_model: one continuous Claude session per episode

scripted_plus_jev.description: Code enumerates the legal actions each turn; Jev's Choice picks among them. No natural-language generation anywhere in the loop.
scripted_plus_jev.execution_model: one Jev call per step, orchestrated entirely by code
scripted_plus_jev.note: tests how far calibrated judgment alone gets you with zero generative reasoning

claude_plus_jev.description: Claude proposes k candidate actions with rationale each turn; Jev arbitrates (Choice among Claude's candidates, always restricted to legal actions supplied by code); confidence gates auto-execute vs escalate.
claude_plus_jev.execution_model: one Claude call + one Jev call per step (plus extra Claude calls on escalation retries)
claude_plus_jev.escalation_rule: if Jev's top-choice confidence < threshold (search this empirically, anchor near 0.75 per BeLazy167/typesafe-mod's shipped default), ask Claude once for different candidates citing the low confidence; if still below threshold after retry, log as 'would escalate to human' rather than guessing -- do not silently pick the low-confidence option

primary_outcomes: illegal_or_hallucinated_action_rate (expected ~0 for both Jev arms by construction; the interesting number is claude_autonomous's rate, and whether claude_plus_jev structurally eliminates it)
secondary_outcomes: escalation_rate (claude_plus_jev only) and human-agreement-rate on escalated cases
calibration_quality: does confidence predict correctness -- Jev's probabilities vs Claude's own declared_uncertainty text, scored against actual outcomes, not just presence/absence of a self-report
cost_usd, split by model (Claude $/token vs Jev $/token are not comparable units -- report both, and a combined total)
wall_seconds, split by model call type (Claude calls are slow/expensive per call; Jev calls are ~300-500ms -- report call counts per model too, not just totals)

context_tokens_used against each model's own ceiling (Jev's measured practical ceiling is ~33k input tokens; report headroom remaining per step, since long episodes may need a summarized/windowed state for Jev specifically)
held_constant: legal-action interface text exposed to whichever model needs it
number of trials per level per arm

analysis.stage_1_pilot: run claude_autonomous on one straightforward and one ambiguous sentinel level, 5x each, to measure Claude's own step-to-step variance on this environment before committing a repeat count -- do not assume E10's N=5 transfers; Jev's variance is already measured (small, from the earlier determinism bench) but Claude's on this task is not
analysis.stage_2_breadth: each level once per arm, across the full level set (straightforward + ambiguous)
analysis.stage_3_repeats: sentinel levels (>=1 straightforward, >=1 ambiguous) repeated N times per arm, N set from stage_1's measured variance
analysis.reporting: break results down by level type (straightforward vs ambiguous), not just aggregated -- the hypothesis is that the arms tie on straightforward levels and diverge on ambiguous ones; an aggregate-only report would hide exactly the result we're looking for

claim_boundary: a configuration effect on this synthetic navigation environment; not a claim of general Claude+Jev superiority or a production guarantee. Extending the result to a real problem (e.g. an agent-action verifier) requires re-running this same protocol on that domain's own tasks.
open_requirements: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY needed to automate claude_autonomous and claude_plus_jev across many trials unattended
confidence threshold for escalation should be searched empirically (start near 0.75), not fixed a priori
level set (straightforward + ambiguous) needs to be authored and BFS-validated for optimal path length before stage_1 pilot runs
